- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >75% increase in 3–5 days) — add 3–8% buffer to prevent overshoot.
- Lagged sentiment (1–2 days prior) often predicts mean reversion — adjust forecast downward if sentiment drops below 0.45.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.3), forecast should be conservative — reduce 30d forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast > true outcome by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid momentum trap.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment > 0.7 but price forecast < 75% of recent high, increase forecast by 5–10% to align with sentiment momentum.
